items.text: Sober spaces
$X$ Hausdorff: $i\colon X\to\tilde X$ is a homeomorphism.
i\ \text{injective}\iff\overline{\{x\}}=\overline{\{y\}}\Rightarrow x=y
Points with the same closure are indistinguishable: pass to the quotient.
Generic point of $Z$: a point whose closure is $Z$.
i\ \text{surjective}\iff\text{every irreducible closed subset has a generic point}
Fails for varieties seen through their $K$-points only; then one adds generic points.
Sober space: every irreducible closed subset has exactly one generic point, i.e. $X\to\tilde X$ bijective (a homeomorphism).
Stalk at an irreducible closed set
$Y\in\tilde X$, $F$ a sheaf on $X$:
F_Y=\varinjlim_{U\cap Y\neq\varnothing}F(U)
Irreducibility makes the system of such $U$ filtering. Left exact, commutes with all direct limits.
$Y=\overline{\{x\}}$: the opens meeting $Y$ are those containing $x$: the usual stalk.
In general: the stalk of $F$ seen on $\tilde X$ at the point $Y$.
\tilde X\ \xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\ \{\text{iso classes of fibre functors } \operatorname{Top}(X)\to\mathbf{Sets}\},\qquad Y\mapsto \varepsilon_Y=(F\mapsto F_Y)
Fibre functor = left exact + commutes with all direct limits. Exercise in SGA 4.
So the points of the sober space are recovered from $\operatorname{Top}(X)$.
A fibre functor has no automorphisms other than the identity: isomorphic ones are identified.
Universal property of $\tilde X$
\operatorname{Hom}(X,\,i(Y))=\operatorname{Hom}(\tilde X,\,Y)\qquad Y\ \text{sober}
$X\mapsto\tilde X$ is left adjoint to the inclusion of sober spaces into spaces.
A map $X\to Y$ sends irreducible closed sets to irreducible sets, whose closures are irreducible: gives $\tilde X\to Y$, unique.
The topology, from the category
\tilde X=\Phi(E),\quad E=\operatorname{Top}(X),\quad \Phi(E)=\{\text{fibre functors}\}/\simeq
For $U\subset e$ a subobject of the final object, a fibre functor sends $U$ to $\varnothing$ or to a point.
\tilde U=\{\varepsilon\in\tilde X:\ \varepsilon(U)\neq\varnothing\}
Fibre functors commute with direct limits and finite limits: the $\tilde U$ are stable under unions and finite intersections: a topology on $\tilde X$.
$X\to\tilde X$ sends a point to its fibre functor: the same map as before.
Subobjects of $e$ = opens of $X$: the topology of $X$ is the inverse image topology.
X\ \text{recoverable from } \operatorname{Top}(X)\iff X\ \text{sober}
Also: $X$ Jacobson (closed points dense in every closed set) $\Rightarrow$ $X$ = closed points of $\tilde X$.
